width.description: Target canvas width. Provide with `height` to place the image on a canvas of exactly this size (canvas mode). Mutually exclusive with the per-side padding args.

right.description: Padding to add to the right (padding mode).

left.description: Padding to add to the left (padding mode).

tools.name: video_concatenate
tools.description: Concatenate videos end-to-end. By default uses hard cuts (fast stream copy). Pass `transition` (e.g., "fade", "wipeleft") to blend clips with xfade crossfades — this implicitly re-encodes and requires identical resolution/frame rate.

inputs.description: Paths to video files to concatenate, in order

output.description: Path for the concatenated output video

reencode.description: If true, re-encode via concat filter (safe for mixed codecs/formats; slower). If false, use concat demuxer (fast; requires identical codecs/resolutions). Ignored when `transition` is set — transitions always re-encode.

transition.description: Optional FFmpeg xfade transition name to blend each pair of clips — e.g., "fade", "wipeleft", "slideup", "circleopen", "dissolve". When set, clips are joined with smooth crossfades instead of hard cuts (implicitly re-encodes). Omit for hard cuts. Inputs must share resolution/frame rate when using transitions; use video_set_resolution first if they don't. See https://ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg-filters.html#xfade for the full list.

transition_duration.description: Duration of each transition in seconds when `transition` is set (typically 0.3–1.5).

tools.name: video_trim
tools.description: Trim a video to a time range. Specify duration_seconds OR end_seconds (not both). Set reencode=true for frame-accurate cuts.

start_seconds.description: Start time in seconds from the beginning

duration_seconds.description: Duration to keep, in seconds. If omitted, uses end_seconds or trims to end.

end_seconds.description: Alternative to duration_seconds — absolute end time in seconds

reencode.description: If true, re-encode (frame-accurate but slower). If false, copy streams (faster but may snap to keyframe boundaries).

tools.name: video_change_aspect_ratio
tools.description: Reframe a video to a target aspect ratio by cropping or padding. Useful for converting landscape → portrait (9:16) for Reels/Shorts.

aspect_ratio.description: Target aspect ratio — known values: "1:1", "4:5", "9:16", "16:9", "3:2", "21:9". Also accepts any "W:H" where W and H are positive integers.

mode.description: "crop" removes edges to fit; "pad" adds bars of pad_color to fit

pad_color.description: Color for padding bars when mode="pad" (e.g., "black", "#RRGGBB")

tools.name: video_convert_format
tools.description: Convert a video to a different container format (mp4/webm/mov/mkv/avi/flv). Re-encodes video/audio to a sensible default for the target container.

output.description: Path for the converted output (format inferred from extension)

format.description: Container format override (mp4, webm, mov, mkv, avi, flv). If omitted, inferred from output extension.

tools.name: video_change_speed
tools.description: Change playback speed. speed > 1 is faster, speed < 1 is slower. preserve_audio requires speed in [0.5, 2.0].

speed.description: Speed multiplier. >1 = faster (e.g., 2.0 is 2× speed). <1 = slower (e.g., 0.5 is half-speed).

preserve_audio.description: If true, pitch-preserving audio scaling (only supports 0.5-2.0 in a single pass). If false, drops audio.

tools.name: video_set_resolution
tools.description: Resize video to a target resolution. Use preset (480p/720p/1080p/1440p/4k) or explicit width/height. preserve_aspect_ratio=true fits within the target box.

preset.description: Resolution preset — one of: "480p", "720p", "1080p", "1440p", "4k". Overrides width/height when set.

preserve_aspect_ratio.description: If true, scales to fit within the target box (aspect preserved). If false, stretches exactly to target (may distort).

tools.name: video_add_transitions
tools.description: Join videos with xfade transitions between each pair. Inputs must share resolution/frame rate; use video_set_resolution first if not. See FFmpeg xfade docs for transition names.

inputs.description: Paths to video files to join with transitions, in order (min 2). Inputs must have identical resolution/frame rate.

transition.description: FFmpeg xfade transition name — e.g., "fade", "wipeleft", "slideup", "circleopen", "dissolve". See https://ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg-filters.html#xfade for the full list.

duration.description: Duration of each transition in seconds (typically 0.5–2).

tools.name: video_add_image_overlay
tools.description: Overlay an image (logo, watermark, badge) on a video. Supports opacity and optional time range.

overlay.description: Path to the overlay image (e.g., logo, watermark)

x.description: Overlay X position. Accepts pixels (10) or FFmpeg expressions ("main_w-overlay_w-10" for right-10).

y.description: Overlay Y position (pixels or FFmpeg expression).

start_seconds.description: Show overlay starting at this time. If omitted, shows from start.

end_seconds.description: Hide overlay after this time. If omitted, shows to end.

tools.name: video_add_text_overlay
tools.description: Burn text onto a video via the drawtext filter. Supports time-bounded display, background box, and custom font file.

text.description: Text to draw on the video

font_file.description: Absolute path to a .ttf/.otf font file. If omitted, uses FFmpeg drawtext default (fontconfig-based; system-default font). For portable/hermetic results, pass an explicit font file path.

x.description: Text X position. Accepts pixels or FFmpeg expressions. Default centers horizontally.

y.description: Text Y position. Accepts pixels or FFmpeg expressions. Default is 40px from bottom.

box.description: Draw a background box behind the text.

box_border_width.description: Padding between text and box edge.

start_seconds.description: Show text starting at this time. If omitted, shows from start.

end_seconds.description: Hide text after this time. If omitted, shows to end.

tools.name: video_add_subtitles
tools.description: Add subtitles from an SRT/VTT/ASS file. burn_in=true renders them into the pixels (always visible); burn_in=false muxes as a soft track (toggleable in player).

subtitle_file.description: Path to an SRT, VTT, or ASS subtitle file.

burn_in.description: If true, renders subtitles into the pixels (always visible). If false, muxes as a soft subtitle track (toggleable in player; only for containers that support it).

force_style.description: ASS style override for burn-in, e.g., "FontName=Arial,FontSize=24,PrimaryColour=&HFFFFFF&,OutlineColour=&H000000&". Only used when burn_in=true.

tools.name: video_add_b_roll
tools.description: Insert a b-roll clip into the main video at a specific time. replace_main_duration=true cuts that segment out of the main (preserving main audio — cutaway style); false inserts additionally (extends length).

main.description: Path to the main video (e.g., talking head)

b_roll.description: Path to the b-roll clip to insert

insert_at_seconds.description: Time in the main video where the b-roll is inserted.

b_roll_duration_seconds.description: How many seconds of the b-roll clip to use (trimmed from b_roll start).

replace_main_duration.description: If true, the b-roll replaces the same duration in the main (keeps main's audio; b-roll becomes a "cutaway"). If false, the b-roll is inserted — extending total length by b_roll_duration.

tools.name: video_set_bitrate
tools.description: Re-encode with a target video and/or audio bitrate. Use two_pass=true for more accurate bitrate targeting on longer clips.

two_pass.description: If true, uses two-pass encoding for more accurate bitrate targeting (slower; requires a temp log file).

tools.name: video_set_codec
tools.description: Re-encode with specific video and/or audio codecs. Supports quality (CRF) and speed (preset) tuning for x264/x265/AV1.

crf.description: Constant Rate Factor (quality). For libx264/libx265: 0 (lossless)–51, typical 18–28. For libvpx-vp9/libaom-av1: 0–63.

tools.name: video_set_frame_rate
tools.description: Change video frame rate. drop_duplicate_frames=true uses the fps filter (preserves duration by dropping/duplicating frames); false uses -r (simpler but may stretch timing).

frame_rate.description: Target frame rate in fps — e.g., 24, 29.97, 30, 60.

drop_duplicate_frames.description: If true, uses the fps filter (frame-accurate; drops/duplicates frames to hit target). If false, uses -r (simpler but may stretch/shrink duration).

tools.name: video_from_image
tools.description: Create a short video clip from a still image — ideal for title cards, end cards, or static intros. Loops the image for duration_seconds and encodes with yuv420p for consumer-player compatibility. Optional audio track can be muxed in; otherwise the clip is silent.

input.description: Path to the source still image (PNG/JPG).

output.description: Path for the output video clip.

duration_seconds.description: Clip duration in seconds — e.g., 2 for a title card, 3 for an end card.

width.description: Resize output to this width. If omitted, uses source width.

height.description: Resize output to this height. If omitted, uses source height.

audio.description: Optional audio track to pair with the image. If omitted, output has no audio (silent clip).

tools.name: video_set_audio
tools.description: Replace (or add) an audio track on a video by muxing in a new audio file. Video stream is stream-copied (no re-encode). Use this after mixing dialogue + music with audio_mix to attach the final soundtrack to a finished video.

audio.description: Path to the audio track to mux in. Replaces any existing audio.

audio_codec.description: Audio codec for the output — "aac" (mp4/mov), "libopus" (webm), or "copy".

shortest.description: If true, output ends when the shorter of video/audio ends. Otherwise, output matches the video length (audio may be padded or truncated).

tools.name: video_make_loop
tools.description: Turn a clip into a seamless loop for loop surfaces (Spotify Canvas, Apple motion art, ambient TikTok/IG loops), or check how visible an existing clip's loop seam is. Modes: `rebound` (forward then reverse), `crossfade` (blend the end into the start), `check` (measure only). Output is always silent H.264, since loop surfaces play over the track. Use max_duration / min_duration for platform windows, e.g. Canvas 3–8s. Every built loop is seam-checked and the result reports it.

input.description: Path to the source video clip.

output.description: Path for the looping output (mp4/mov; encoded H.264 yuv420p, no audio). Required for `rebound` and `crossfade`; ignored for `check`.

mode.description: `rebound`: play forward then in reverse (the Spotify Canvas "rebound" style), dropping the duplicated turn-around frames so neither end stalls. Output is about twice the source length. `crossfade`: blend the last `crossfade_seconds` into the first, so a clip whose first and last frames differ loops without a jump. Output is `crossfade_seconds` shorter than the source. `check`: build nothing; measure how visible the input's own last→first seam is, e.g. to test whether a first=last-frame generation actually closed the loop.

crossfade_seconds.description: Crossfade length in seconds (`crossfade` mode). The source must be longer than twice this. Longer blends hide bigger differences but show more ghosting.

max_duration.description: Upper bound on the loop length in seconds (e.g. 8 for Spotify Canvas). Applied by trimming the SOURCE before the loop is built, so the result stays seamless; the finished loop is never cut mid-cycle.

min_duration.description: Lower bound on the output length in seconds (e.g. 3 for Spotify Canvas). Reached by repeating whole loop cycles, which keeps the seam clean. If that overshoots `max_duration`, the seamless length is kept and a warning is returned.

tools.name: audio_info
tools.description: Get audio metadata: duration, codec, sample rate, channels, bitrate, container format, and file size. The audio counterpart to the image-only `info` tool — use it to inspect a file before or after a transform instead of shelling out to ffprobe.

input.description: Path to the audio file to probe (or a video file — the first audio stream is reported).

tools.name: audio_extract_from_video
tools.description: Extract the audio track from a video file. Use codec="copy" to avoid re-encoding when the source audio codec is compatible with the target container.

input.description: Path to the source video file

output.description: Path for the extracted audio (format inferred from extension)

codec.description: Audio codec override (e.g., "libmp3lame", "aac", "libopus", "copy"). If omitted, picks a sensible default per output extension.

bitrate.description: Target audio bitrate — e.g., "192k", "320k". If omitted, uses encoder default.

tools.name: audio_normalize
tools.description: Normalize audio loudness. mode="loudnorm" uses EBU R128 (recommended for streaming/broadcast); mode="peak" uses a simple volume-based peak normalization.

input.description: Path to the source audio (or video with audio)

mode.description: "loudnorm" = EBU R128 loudness normalization (broadcast/streaming standard). "peak" = simple peak normalization via volume filter (legacy; less accurate).

target_lufs.description: Target integrated loudness in LUFS for loudnorm mode. Common targets: -14 (Spotify/YouTube), -16 (Apple Music), -23 (EBU broadcast).

target_peak_db.description: Target true peak in dBTP for loudnorm mode or peak target for peak mode. Typical: -1.0 or -2.0.

tools.name: audio_convert_format
tools.description: Convert audio between container formats (mp3/aac/wav/flac/ogg/m4a/opus). Re-encodes with a sensible codec default per target format.

output.description: Path for the converted output (format inferred from extension)

format.description: Container format override (mp3, aac, wav, flac, ogg, m4a, opus). If omitted, inferred from output extension.

codec.description: Codec override. If omitted, picks a sensible default for the target format (e.g., libmp3lame for mp3, libopus for opus).

tools.name: audio_convert_properties
tools.description: Change multiple audio properties in one pass — sample rate, channel count, bitrate, and/or codec. More efficient than chaining single-property tools.

sample_rate.description: Target sample rate in Hz — typical values: 22050, 44100, 48000, 96000.

codec.description: Codec override. If omitted, picks a default for the output extension.

tools.name: audio_set_bitrate
tools.description: Re-encode audio at a target bitrate. Useful for reducing file size (e.g., 320k → 128k for web delivery).

codec.description: Codec override. If omitted, picks a default for the output extension.

tools.name: audio_set_channels
tools.description: Downmix or upmix audio to a target channel count. 2→1 is a proper stereo-to-mono downmix; 1→2 duplicates the mono channel.

codec.description: Codec override. If omitted, picks a default for the output extension.

tools.name: audio_set_sample_rate
tools.description: Resample audio to a target sample rate. Uses FFmpeg's high-quality resampler by default.

sample_rate.description: Target sample rate in Hz — typical values: 22050, 44100, 48000, 96000.

codec.description: Codec override. If omitted, picks a default for the output extension.

tools.name: audio_remove_silence
tools.description: Trim silence from audio. remove="both" trims leading/trailing silence (most common); "all" also removes silent sections within the audio (may sound unnatural).

threshold_db.description: Silence threshold in dB (negative; closer to 0 = more aggressive). Typical: -40 (loose), -50 (balanced), -60 (strict).

min_silence_duration.description: Minimum silence duration in seconds to trim (avoids cutting natural speech pauses).

remove.description: "start" = leading silence only. "end" = trailing only. "both" = start + end. "all" = also removes silence within the audio (may sound unnatural).

tools.name: audio_mix
tools.description: Mix 2+ audio tracks into one output with per-track volume and optional delay. Supports sidechain ducking: when `duck_to` and `duck_against_track` are set, the specified track(s) are lowered (dB) whenever track 0 is audible — ideal for ducking a music bed under dialogue.

input.description: Path to an audio track (or any file with audio).

volume.description: Linear volume multiplier applied before mixing — 1.0 = unchanged, 0.3 = 30%, 0 = silent. Default 1.0.

delay_seconds.description: Delay this track by N seconds before it enters the mix (default 0).

tracks.description: Ordered list of tracks to mix (2+). Track 0 is the reference for ducking.

output.description: Path for the mixed output audio.

duration.description: "longest" = output length = longest input (pads shorter with silence). "shortest" = stops at shortest. "first" = matches track 0.

duck_to.description: If set, activates sidechain ducking: lowers `duck_against_track` by this many dB whenever track 0 (voice) is audible. Typical: -10 to -18. Omit for no ducking.

duck_against_track.description: Index of the track to duck (1-based, referring to tracks[1] and later). Required when duck_to is set. Usually the music-bed track.

duck_attack_ms.description: Sidechain attack time in ms — how fast the duck engages when voice starts.

duck_release_ms.description: Sidechain release time in ms — how fast volume recovers after voice ends.

tools.name: audio_pad
tools.description: Prepend and/or append silence to an audio file. Specify pad_start_seconds, pad_end_seconds, or both (at least one required). Float seconds supported (e.g., 0.25). Re-encodes via the output extension default codec.

input.description: Path to the source audio (or video with audio).

output.description: Path for the padded output (format inferred from extension).

pad_start_seconds.description: Seconds of silence to prepend to the audio. Float OK (e.g., 0.25). Specify pad_start_seconds and/or pad_end_seconds — at least one is required.

pad_end_seconds.description: Seconds of silence to append to the audio. Float OK (e.g., 1.5). Specify pad_start_seconds and/or pad_end_seconds — at least one is required.

codec.description: Codec override. If omitted, picks a default for the output extension.

tools.name: gemini_generate_image
tools.description: Generate images from a text prompt via Google Imagen. Returns 1-4 images saved to the output path. Uses GOOGLE_API_KEY env var.

model.description: Imagen model ID — REQUIRED, no default. Google deprecated Imagen 4 (shutdown notice on imagen-4.0-generate-001), so artificer ships no default here. Prefer gemini_nanobanana_generate_image; see gemini_image_prompt_guide for the migration map. Pin a model via ARTIFICER_IMAGEN_MODEL to restore a default.

prompt.description: Text description of the image to generate.

output.description: Output path for the generated image (e.g., "./output.png"). When number_of_images > 1, files are numbered (output_1.png, output_2.png, ...).

negative_prompt.description: What to discourage in the generated image.

safety_filter_level.description: Safety filter — "BLOCK_LOW_AND_ABOVE", "BLOCK_MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE", "BLOCK_ONLY_HIGH", "BLOCK_NONE". Omit to use API default; note the Gemini Developer API (aistudio keys) currently only accepts BLOCK_LOW_AND_ABOVE.

enhance_prompt.description: If true, Gemini rewrites the prompt for better results. The enhanced prompt is returned in the response.

tools.name: gemini_edit_image
tools.description: Edit an existing image with a text instruction via Google Imagen. Supports inpainting, outpainting, style transfer, background swap, and more.

model.description: Imagen editing model ID — REQUIRED, no default. The Imagen family is deprecated; prefer gemini_nanobanana_generate_image with reference_images for edits. Pin a model via ARTIFICER_IMAGEN_EDIT_MODEL to restore a default.

prompt.description: Description of the edit to apply.

image.description: Path to the source image to edit.

output.description: Output path for the edited image. Numbered if number_of_images > 1.

mask_image.description: Path to a mask image (white = edit region, black = preserve). Required for inpaint/outpaint modes.

tools.name: gemini_upscale_image
tools.description: Upscale an image 2x or 4x via Google Imagen. REQUIRES VERTEX AI — this method is not available on the Gemini Developer API, so a GOOGLE_API_KEY alone will not work. Set GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT (and optionally GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION) plus Application Default Credentials.

model.description: Upscale model ID. Default: imagen-4.0-upscale-preview (override via ARTIFICER_IMAGEN_UPSCALE_MODEL env var). Note: upscaling is Vertex-AI-only — GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT must be set.

image.description: Path to the image to upscale.

output.description: Output path for the upscaled image.

tools.name: gemini_generate_video
tools.description: Generate a video from a text prompt (text-to-video) or from a text prompt + input image (image-to-video) via Google Veo. Long-running — polls until complete or timeout. Uses GOOGLE_API_KEY env var.

model.description: Veo model ID. Pass any valid model string. Default: veo-2.0-generate-001 (override via ARTIFICER_VEO_MODEL env var).

prompt.description: Text description of the video to generate.

output.description: Output path for the generated video (e.g., "./output.mp4").

image.description: Path to an input image for image-to-video generation. When provided, the video starts from this image.

duration_seconds.description: Video duration in seconds. Model-dependent; Veo 2.0 supports 5-8s.

person_generation.description: "dont_allow" or "allow_adult". Omit to use API default.

generate_audio.description: If true, generate audio alongside video (model-dependent).

enhance_prompt.description: If true, Gemini rewrites the prompt for better results.

poll_interval_seconds.description: How often to check if video generation is complete (seconds).

poll_timeout_seconds.description: Maximum time to wait for video generation (seconds). Default 5 minutes.

tools.name: gemini_omni_generate_video
tools.description: Generate video via Google Gemini Omni Flash (Interactions API). Text-to-video, image-to-video, or reference-to-video, plus stateful conversational editing of a previous result via previous_interaction_id. Output carries NATIVE AUDIO (speech/music/SFX) generated in the same pass, with no flag to disable it — describe the audio you want in the prompt, or strip the track downstream if you are laying your own music under the clip. Long-running; polls until complete or timeout. Uses GOOGLE_API_KEY env var.

model.description: Gemini Omni video model ID. Default: gemini-omni-1.1-flash (override via ARTIFICER_OMNI_VIDEO_MODEL env var).

prompt.description: Text prompt describing the video, or the edit to apply.

output.description: Output path for the generated video (e.g. "./clip.mp4").

image.description: Optional source image for image-to-video. Local path or URL.

reference_images.description: Optional reference images for reference-to-video (subject / style consistency). Local paths or URLs.

task.description: Explicit task mode. Omit to let the model infer it from the prompt and attached media. Use "edit" together with previous_interaction_id for conversational editing.

aspect_ratio.description: Aspect ratio — "16:9" or "9:16". Omit for the model default.

duration_seconds.description: Clip length in seconds (3-10). This tool does not expose the API extend task yet — concatenate clips with video_concatenate for longer pieces.

previous_interaction_id.description: Interaction id returned by a prior call. Supplying it makes this a stateful follow-up edit of that result ("swap the character", "relight the scene") instead of a fresh generation.

poll_interval_seconds.description: How often to poll the interaction for completion (seconds).

poll_timeout_seconds.description: Maximum time to wait for generation (seconds). Default 5 minutes.

tools.name: gemini_nanobanana_generate_image
tools.description: Generate or edit an image via Gemini nano-banana (default gemini-3.1-flash-image). Pass reference_images for edit/composite/style-transfer, and image_size ("2K"/"4K") for more than the ~1K default. The file format follows the output extension (png/jpg/webp/gif), converting when the model returns a different encoding. Uses GOOGLE_API_KEY.

model.description: Gemini image model ID (nano-banana family). Default: gemini-3.1-flash-image (Nano Banana 2). Siblings: gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image (cheaper), gemini-3-pro-image (highest fidelity), gemini-2.5-flash-image (previous generation). Override the default via ARTIFICER_NANOBANANA_MODEL env var.

prompt.description: Text prompt. If reference_images are provided, describe the edit or composition.

output.description: Output path for the generated image (e.g., "./output.png").

reference_images.description: Optional local paths to reference images. When provided, nano-banana uses them as visual context — enabling edits, composites, style transfer, and reference-guided generation.

image_size.description: Output resolution tier. Omit for the API default, 1K (e.g. 896×1200 at 3:4). "2K" and "4K" cost more per image; see gemini_nanobanana_prompt_guide for per-tier pricing. Supported by the Gemini 3 image models; older models may reject it.

include_text.description: If true, request text modality alongside image — any narration returned is included in the response.

tools.name: gemini_generate_speech
tools.description: Generate natural-sounding speech from text via Gemini TTS (gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts by default). Returns PCM wrapped in WAV; other extensions are transcoded via ffmpeg. Uses GOOGLE_API_KEY.

model.description: Gemini TTS model ID. Default: gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts (override via ARTIFICER_TTS_MODEL env var). Also valid: gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts.

text.description: Text to speak. Keep under ~1000 chars per call for best results. May include natural-language style prompts inline (e.g., "Say warmly: Hello baker").

output.description: Output audio path. .wav is emitted natively; any other extension is transcoded via ffmpeg (requires ffmpeg on PATH).

voice.description: Prebuilt voice name — "Kore" (warm, calm), "Puck" (upbeat), "Zephyr" (bright), "Charon" (informative), "Fenrir" (excitable), "Leda" (youthful), "Aoede" (breezy), "Orus" (firm), "Sage" (clear). See Gemini TTS docs for full list. When omitted, falls back to ARTIFICER_BRAND_SPEC.tts.voice if set, otherwise "Kore".

language_code.description: Optional ISO-639-1 language code (e.g., "en-US"). Usually auto-detected.

style.description: Optional style prefix prepended to the text as a natural-language instruction (e.g., "In a warm, encouraging tone"). Concatenated with a colon to the text.

tools.name: gemini_generate_music
tools.description: Generate music synchronously via Lyria 3 (batch). Returns a 30s clip for lyria-3-clip-preview or up to ~2min (prompt-driven) for lyria-3-pro-preview. Uses GOOGLE_API_KEY. For live/interactive streaming, use gemini_generate_music_live.

model.description: Lyria 3 model ID. Default: lyria-3-clip-preview (fixed 30-second clip). Also valid: lyria-3-pro-preview (up to ~2 minutes, duration controllable via prompt; emits WAV instead of MP3). Override via ARTIFICER_LYRIA_MODEL env var.

prompt.description: Music description — genre, mood, instruments, tempo. E.g., "upbeat indie folk with acoustic guitar and claps, 110 bpm, warm". Pro model supports timestamps like "[0:00-0:15] calm intro, [0:15-0:30] build to drop" for structured tracks.

output.description: Output audio path. Native format: MP3 for clip, WAV for Pro. Other extensions transcoded via ffmpeg.

negative_prompt.description: Elements to avoid — appended to the prompt as "Avoid: ...". Note: Lyria 3 does not expose a dedicated negative_prompt field like Lyria 2, so this is prompt-engineered guidance rather than a guarantee.

tools.name: gemini_generate_music_live
tools.description: Generate music via Lyria RealTime (WebSocket streaming). Opens a session, sends weighted prompt, collects audio chunks for duration_seconds, then force-closes. Enforces a hard wall-clock timeout so the tool will always return. Uses GOOGLE_API_KEY. For simpler one-shot music beds, prefer gemini_generate_music (Lyria 3 batch).

model.description: Lyria RealTime model ID. Default: models/lyria-realtime-exp. Override via ARTIFICER_LYRIA_LIVE_MODEL env var. This tool opens a WebSocket session, collects audio for duration_seconds, then force-closes.

prompt.description: Music description — genre, mood, instruments, tempo. Sent as weightedPrompts[0] with weight 1.0.

output.description: Output audio path. .wav is emitted natively; other extensions transcoded via ffmpeg.

duration_seconds.description: How long to capture audio before closing the session (seconds). Capped at 120s to avoid runaway sessions.

temperature.description: Audio variance. Higher = more variance. Range 0.0–3.0.

guidance.description: How closely the model follows prompts. Range 0.0–6.0.

tools.name: fal_generate_video
tools.description: Generate or transform a video via any fal-hosted video model: text/image/audio-to-video, and video-to-video (upscale, restore, edit, restyle, lip-sync) via the `video` input. Transport tool only — pass an explicit `model` (no server-side default). Use `model_catalog` to discover available models and the matching `*_prompt_guide` tool to learn the per-model prompt structure. Uses FAL_KEY env var.

model.description: Fal-hosted model id, e.g. "fal-ai/wan/v2.7/image-to-video", "fal-ai/kling-video/ai-avatar/v2/pro", "veed/fabric-1.0". Required — no server-side default. Discover available models via `model_catalog`; read the model-specific prompt guide before calling.

prompt.description: Text prompt describing the desired video. Optional for image-to-video and audio-driven models where the image or audio carries most of the signal; required for text-to-video.

image.description: Input image URL or local path. Public HTTPS URLs pass through to fal unchanged; gs:// / s3:// / local paths are uploaded to fal storage first.

audio.description: Input audio URL or local path for audio-driven models (Wan 2.7, Kling AI Avatar, veed/fabric). Same resolution rules as `image`.

video.description: Input video URL or local path → `video_url`, for video-to-video models (upscale, restore, edit, restyle, lip-sync). Same resolution rules as `image`. Many v2v models bill per second of INPUT video; check the prompt guide.

duration_seconds.description: Target video duration in seconds. Integer only — passing a string will fail at schema validation (regression guard for a real 422 observed during the Q2 bake-off). For audio-driven models like Wan 2.7, pass Math.ceil(audio_seconds) to avoid truncation.

aspect_ratio.description: Model-dependent aspect ratio hint, e.g. "16:9", "9:16", "1:1". Pass-through — not all models accept this parameter.

resolution.description: Model-dependent resolution hint, e.g. "480p", "720p", "1080p". Pass-through. NOTE: Wan 2.7 audio-driven mode requires "720p" explicitly; omitting it defaults to 1080p and exceeds fal's generation budget (see wan_video_prompt_guide).

negative_prompt.description: Content to discourage. Pass-through — model support varies.

extra_params.description: Free-form passthrough to the fal payload for any model-specific knobs not covered above (seed, negative_prompt variations, face_swap settings, etc.). Keys are spread as top-level input fields. Unknown keys go to fal as-is; fal responds with 422 if the model rejects them — that error surfaces verbatim, we do not silently drop.

extra_files.description: File-bearing extension to extra_params. Each value is treated like the structural `image` / `audio` args — public http(s) passes through, gs:// / s3:// / file:// / local paths are uploaded to fal storage — and the resulting URL is merged into the fal payload under the same key. Use this for secondary file inputs (start_image_url, end_image_url, reference_image_urls[], mask_url, etc.) that fal models expose only via extra params. extra_files wins over extra_params on key collision because the caller deliberately marked those keys as files.

poll_timeout_seconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait for the fal job before giving up. Default 300 (matches gemini_generate_video). Fal's subscribe() polls the queue internally — there is no separate poll interval knob.

tools.name: fal_generate_image
tools.description: Generate, edit, upscale or cut out images via any fal-hosted image model. Transport tool: pass an explicit `model` (no server-side default); use `model_catalog` (capability "image") to discover models and the matching prompt guide to learn their inputs. Images are saved exactly as the model returns them; choose a format with extra_params.output_format where the model supports it. Uses FAL_KEY env var.

model.description: Fal-hosted image model id, e.g. "bytedance/seedream/v5/pro/text-to-image", "fal-ai/flux-2-pro/edit", "topaz/upscale/image/precision". Required, no server-side default. Discover models via `model_catalog` (capability "image") and read the matching prompt guide first.

prompt.description: Text prompt. Required by generation and most edit models; omit it for prompt-less task models (upscalers, background removal).

output.description: Output URI for the first image (e.g. "./out.png", "gs://bucket/out.png"). Additional images are saved beside it as <name>_2, <name>_3, …. The file holds exactly what the model returned; use an extension that matches the model's output format (set it with extra_params.output_format where supported).

image.description: Single input image → `image_url` (upscalers, background removal, single-image edit models). Public HTTPS URLs pass through; local paths and gs:// / s3:// URIs are uploaded to fal storage first.

images.description: Input / reference images → `image_urls` (multi-reference edit and composition models such as Seedream edit, FLUX.2 edit, Nano Banana edit). Same resolution rules as `image`.

mask.description: Mask image → `mask_url` for inpainting and object removal. Same resolution rules as `image`. Models that name it differently (e.g. `mask_image_url`) take it via extra_files.

aspect_ratio.description: Aspect ratio hint, e.g. "1:1", "3:4", "16:9". Pass-through; model support varies.

image_size.description: fal image_size: a preset such as "square_hd", "portrait_4_3", "landscape_16_9", "auto_2K", or an explicit { width, height }. Pass-through; accepted values vary by model.

resolution.description: Resolution tier on models that use one instead of image_size, e.g. "1K" / "2K" / "4K" (Nano Banana, Kling Image) or "1k" / "2k" (Grok Imagine). Pass-through.

num_images.description: How many images to generate, on models that support it. Each is saved separately.

negative_prompt.description: Content to discourage. Pass-through; many current models ignore or reject it.

extra_params.description: Passthrough for model-specific knobs not covered above: output_format, seed, upscale_factor, guidance, safety settings, etc. Keys are spread as top-level fal input fields. Keys the model does not accept trigger a stderr warning (fal drops them silently).

extra_files.description: File-bearing extra_params: each value is resolved like `image` (uploaded if local) and merged into the payload under its key. Use for secondary file inputs such as reference_image_urls, person_image_url, garment_image_urls, mask_image_url. Wins over extra_params on key collision.

poll_timeout_seconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait for the fal job before giving up. Default 300.

tools.name: fal_classify_text
tools.description: Classify text for safety via a fal-hosted safety model. Returns {safe, label, categories, raw}. When exactly one non-stub safety.text entry exists in the catalog, `model` auto-defaults to it — otherwise `model` is required, which is the case today (fal retired Qwen 3 Guard on 2026-08-15 and hosts no replacement classifier). Uses FAL_KEY env var.

model.description: Fal safety model id. Optional when exactly one non-stub safety.text entry is in the catalog — that entry auto-defaults. Required otherwise, which is the situation today: fal retired Qwen 3 Guard on 2026-08-15 and currently hosts no safety classifier, so the catalog has no safety entry and this argument must be supplied. Call `model_catalog` with capability:"safety" to check whether one has returned.

tools.name: fal_generate_speech
tools.description: Generate speech via any fal-hosted TTS, voice-clone, or dialogue model. Transport tool — pass explicit `model`. Returns JSON with `audio_uri` (when audio was generated) and `custom_voice_id` (when the model returned one, e.g. voice-cloning). Uses FAL_KEY env var.

model.description: Fal-hosted speech model id, e.g. "fal-ai/elevenlabs/tts/turbo-v2.5", "fal-ai/minimax/speech-2.8-hd", "fal-ai/minimax/voice-clone", "fal-ai/dia-tts". Required — no server-side default. Discover via `model_catalog` with capability:"speech"; read the matching prompt guide before calling.

text.description: Text to synthesize. Required for straight TTS models; optional-to-empty for voice-clone models where the primary payload is reference audio. Passes through as the `text` fal input key.

output.description: Output URI for the generated audio (e.g., "./out.mp3", "gs://bucket/speech.mp3"). Some voice-clone models return no audio by default — in that case the output file is skipped and the response reports `voice_id` only.

voice.description: Named voice id. Model-specific — for ElevenLabs this is a voice name like "Rachel"; for MiniMax it is a voice id string. Passes through as the `voice` fal input key. Omit for models that do not accept a voice arg (dialogue models, voice-design).

reference_audio.description: Audio input URL or local path (voice-clone reference sample, dialogue scene guidance, etc.). Public HTTPS URLs pass through; gs:// / s3:// / local paths are uploaded to fal storage. Passes to fal as `audio_url` — override to a different field name via `extra_params` if the model requires it.

extra_params.description: Free-form passthrough for model-specific knobs (stability, similarity_boost, language_code, apply_text_normalization, etc.). Keys spread as top-level fal input fields. Structural args (text, voice, audio_url) win on collision; fal returns 422 for unknown keys.

extra_files.description: File-bearing extension to extra_params. Each value is uploaded through fal storage (or passed through if already https) and the resulting URL is merged into the fal payload under the same key. Use for secondary audio refs (e.g. dialogue scene guidance) the model exposes only via extra params. extra_files wins on key collision with extra_params.

poll_timeout_seconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait for the fal job. Default 300 (matches the video transports). Fal's subscribe() polls internally — no separate interval knob.

tools.name: fal_generate_music
tools.description: Generate music, songs, or sound effects via any fal-hosted text-to-audio model. Transport tool — pass explicit `model`. Covers music.general / music.song / music.sfx sub-classes in the catalog. Returns JSON with `audio` (written output) and `source_url`. Uses FAL_KEY env var.

model.description: Fal-hosted music / sfx model id, e.g. "fal-ai/elevenlabs/music", "fal-ai/lyria2", "fal-ai/stable-audio-25/text-to-audio", "fal-ai/minimax-music/v2.6" (song with lyrics), "fal-ai/elevenlabs/sound-effects/v2", "cassetteai/sound-effects-generator". Required. Discover via `model_catalog` with capability:"music"; read the matching prompt guide for duration / lyrics / format specifics.

prompt.description: Text description of the music or sound effect to generate. Optional on composition-plan models (Eleven Music supports a structured `composition_plan` via `extra_params` instead) but required on most.

output.description: Output URI for the generated audio.

lyrics.description: Lyrics for song generation (MiniMax Music 2.6, Eleven Music song mode). Passes as `lyrics` to fal. Ignored by instrumental-only models.

reference_audio.description: Audio reference for style-transfer models. Public HTTPS passes through; gs:// / s3:// / local paths are uploaded to fal storage. Maps to fal `audio_url`.

extra_params.description: Free-form passthrough for model-specific knobs (music_length_ms, force_instrumental, output_format, duration_seconds, composition_plan, etc.). Keys spread as top-level fal input fields. Structural args win on collision.

extra_files.description: File-bearing extension to extra_params. Each value is uploaded through fal storage (or passed through if already https) and the resulting URL is merged into the fal payload under the same key. Use for secondary audio refs the model exposes only via extra params. extra_files wins on key collision with extra_params.

tools.name: fal_transcribe
tools.description: Transcribe audio via any fal-hosted ASR model. Transport tool — pass explicit `model`. Returns JSON with `text`, `language`, `words[]` (scribe only — word-level timing for karaoke), `segments[]` (whisper/wizper — segment timing), and the model-specific `raw` payload. Uses FAL_KEY env var. Recommended default for karaoke captions: fal-ai/elevenlabs/speech-to-text/scribe-v2.

model.description: Fal-hosted ASR model id, e.g. "fal-ai/elevenlabs/speech-to-text/scribe-v2" (recommended for karaoke — word-level timing), "fal-ai/whisper" (segment-level), "fal-ai/wizper" (Whisper v3 fal-optimized), "fal-ai/elevenlabs/speech-to-text" (Scribe v1), "fal-ai/speech-to-text", "fal-ai/speech-to-text/turbo", "fal-ai/cohere-transcribe". Required — no server-side default. Discover via `model_catalog` with capability:"transcription"; read the matching prompt guide before calling.

audio.description: Audio input — public HTTPS URL passes through; gs:// / s3:// / local paths are uploaded to fal storage. Maps to fal `audio_url`.

extra_params.description: Free-form passthrough for model-specific knobs (language / language_code, diarize, keyterms, batch_size, num_speakers, chunk_level, max_segment_len, prompt, task, tag_audio_events, etc.). Keys spread as top-level fal input fields. Structural args win on collision.

extra_files.description: File-bearing extension to extra_params. Each value is uploaded through fal storage (or passed through if already https) and the resulting URL is merged into the fal payload under the same key. Rarely needed for ASR (audio is the only structural input) — included for symmetry with the other fal transports. extra_files wins on key collision with extra_params.

poll_timeout_seconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait for the fal job. Default 300 — same as the other fal transports.

tools.name: fal_separate_audio
tools.description: Split a mixed track into stems (vocals, drums, bass, other, …) via a fal-hosted separation model such as Demucs. Writes one file per stem into output_dir as <basename>-<stem>.<ext> and returns the stem → path map. Use for an isolated vocal (lip-sync, karaoke timing, cleaner transcription) or instrumental versions. Uses FAL_KEY env var.

model.description: Fal-hosted separation model id, e.g. "fal-ai/demucs". Required, no server-side default. Discover via `model_catalog` (capability "audio") and read the matching prompt guide.

audio.description: Mixed audio to separate → `audio_url`. Public HTTPS URLs pass through; local paths and gs:// / s3:// URIs are uploaded to fal storage first.

output_dir.description: Directory (local path or storage URI such as gs://bucket/stems) to write the stems into. Each stem is saved as <basename>-<stem>.<ext>, e.g. song-vocals.wav.

basename.description: File name prefix for the stems. Defaults to the input file name without its extension.

stems.description: Which stems to return → `stems`, e.g. ["vocals"] for an isolated vocal. Omit for all of them. Accepted names are model-specific (Demucs: vocals, drums, bass, other, guitar, piano; the last two only with its 6-stem network).

extra_params.description: Model-specific knobs spread into the fal input, e.g. Demucs {"model": "htdemucs_ft", "output_format": "wav"}. Note that a model's own `model` input (its network choice) goes here; the top-level `model` arg is the fal endpoint.

poll_timeout_seconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait for the fal job. Default 600; separation of a full song can take minutes.

tools.name: align_text_to_audio
tools.description: Forced alignment: time a KNOWN transcript (lyrics, script, voiceover) against its audio. Returns word-level and line-level start/end times, flags words the aligner matched poorly, and can write LRC (synced lyrics), SRT (subtitles) or JSON. Unlike ASR (fal_transcribe), the words are exactly your text, so proper nouns and lyrics are never misheard. Lines come from the text's own line breaks. Default model: fal's ElevenLabs forced aligner ($0.22 per started hour of audio). Uses FAL_KEY.

audio.description: Audio to align (vocal, voiceover, narration). Public HTTPS URLs pass through; local paths and gs:// / s3:// URIs are uploaded to fal storage. For songs, align the isolated vocal stem (fal_separate_audio) for cleaner timing.

text.description: The known transcript: lyrics, script or voiceover text, exactly as spoken. Line breaks matter: each non-empty line becomes one timed line (a lyric line or caption).

model.description: Forced-alignment model. Default: fal-ai/elevenlabs/forced-alignment (ElevenLabs, the only aligner fal hosts; $0.22 per hour of audio, rounded UP to a whole hour, so each call costs at least $0.22).

output.description: Optional file to write (local path or storage URI). Format comes from `format`, or from the extension: .lrc (synced lyrics), .srt (subtitles), .json (full detail). The JSON summary is returned either way.

format.description: Output file format. Defaults to the output extension, then json.

extra_params.description: Passthrough for model-specific knobs, spread into the fal input.

poll_timeout_seconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait for the fal job. Default 600.

tools.name: fal_upload
tools.description: Upload a local file (or gs:// / s3:// / file:// URI) to fal storage and return the resulting HTTPS URL. Public http(s) URLs are passed through unchanged. Use this to supply secondary image / audio inputs (e.g. Kling O3 start_frame + end_frame, multi-image reference-to-video models) where the URL must be embedded inside `extra_params`. For one-shot calls you can pass an `extra_files` map directly to any `fal_*` transport instead. Uses FAL_KEY env var.

source.description: File to expose to fal. Use this when a fal model needs a secondary image / audio / video reference (start_frame, end_frame, ref images, etc.) that must be supplied via `extra_params`.

background_color.description: Background color for assets that need padding (hex).

tools.description: Create a social media carousel from a set of images. Resizes each to uniform dimensions and optionally adds caption bars. Outputs numbered slides ready for posting.

captions.description: Caption text per slide (same length as images). If omitted, no caption overlay.

caption_background.description: Caption bar background color with alpha (e.g., "#00000080" for 50% black).

font_file.description: Path to a .ttf/.otf font file for captions. Uses ImageMagick default if omitted.

tools.name: workflow_carousel_compose

content.description: The text to render. Supports multi-line via newlines.

font.description: Font path or name. Overrides brand.font and ARTIFICER_BRAND_SPEC.fonts.regular for this element.

color.description: Text color. When omitted, falls back to ARTIFICER_BRAND_SPEC.colors.primary, else "black".

box_width.description: If set with box_height, auto-wraps text via caption: instead of annotate.

background.description: Undercolor for the text (annotate mode only).

source.description: Path or URI to the image to composite.

elements.description: Elements to draw in order (later elements on top).

slides.description: Ordered list of slides to render.

output_dir.description: Directory (local path or gs://) for slide outputs.

font.description: Default font path for text elements.

tools.name: workflow_talking_head
tools.description: Process a talking-head video in one call: trim → insert b-roll cutaway → burn subtitles → normalize audio. Each step is optional — skip by omitting its params.

input.description: Path to the raw talking-head video.

output.description: Path for the final processed video.

trim_start_seconds.description: Trim: start time in seconds. If omitted, no trimming.

b_roll.description: Path to a b-roll clip. If provided, inserted as a cutaway (keeps main audio).

b_roll_insert_at_seconds.description: Time in the main video to insert b-roll. Required when b_roll is set.

b_roll_duration_seconds.description: How many seconds of b-roll to use. Required when b_roll is set.

subtitle_file.description: Path to an SRT/VTT/ASS subtitle file. If provided, subtitles are burned in.

normalize_audio.description: If true, normalize audio to target_lufs via EBU R128 loudnorm.

target_lufs.description: Target loudness in LUFS when normalize_audio=true. -14 for YouTube/Spotify, -16 for Apple.

tools.name: workflow_ad_creative_set

background.description: Path to the background image (will be resized/cropped per banner size).

font_file.description: Path to a .ttf/.otf font file. Uses ImageMagick default if omitted.

sizes.description: Custom banner sizes. Default: leaderboard (728x90), medium-rectangle (300x250), wide-skyscraper (160x600), mobile-banner (320x50), large-rectangle (336x280), half-page (300x600).

tools.name: workflow_ig_reel

clips.description: Ordered list of video clip paths to concatenate (1+).

output.description: Path for the finished IG Reel MP4.

image.description: Path to the title-card image (will be scaled to 1080×1920).

duration_seconds.description: How long to display the title card in seconds.

audio.description: Optional short audio sting/music to pair with the title card.

title_card.description: Optional title card shown before the body clips.

end_card.description: Optional end card shown after the body clips.

transition.description: FFmpeg xfade transition between body clips (e.g., "fade", "dissolve"). Omit for hard cuts.

transition_duration.description: Transition duration in seconds (used when `transition` is set).

captions_srt.description: Optional path to an SRT file for burned-in captions.

image.description: Watermark image path (SVG or raster). When omitted, falls back to ARTIFICER_BRAND_SPEC.logo.watermark → logo.wordmark → logo.icon.

watermark.description: Optional watermark / brand lower-third overlaid on the entire reel. Pass an empty `{}` to apply the brand spec watermark with defaults.

volume.description: Linear volume for the music bed (0–1). Typical: 0.2–0.35.

duck_to.description: If set, ducks the music bed by this many dB whenever dialogue is audible (sidechain). Typical: -12.

music.description: Optional music bed mixed under the dialogue audio.

fps.description: Output frame rate (30 recommended for Reels).

image.description: Watermark image path (SVG or raster). When omitted, falls back to ARTIFICER_BRAND_SPEC.logo.watermark → logo.wordmark → logo.icon.

watermark.description: Optional watermark / brand lower-third overlaid on the entire reel. Pass an empty `{}` to apply the brand spec watermark with defaults.

volume.description: Linear volume for the music bed (0–1). Typical: 0.2–0.35.

tools.name: model_catalog
tools.description: List available media-generation models grouped by capability and sub-class. Returns logical model slugs, prompt guide tool names, and access routes (provider + transport tool + wire-level model id + cost). Music entries also carry `vocals` ("vocal_capable" or "instrumental_only") — the sub-class says what a model is for, `vocals` says whether it can sing. Call this first when you need to pick a model for a task; then call the relevant prompt_guide, then the access route's transport tool. Routes the provider has deprecated — which still answer but silently serve a different model — are excluded. Use `include_unavailable: true` to see those plus models whose API keys aren't configured.

capability.description: Optional filter — restrict the response to a single capability (video, image, music, speech, audio, safety, transcription). `audio` holds audio-processing models such as stem separation.

include_unavailable.description: If true, include routes whose API keys are not configured, whose transport tool is not yet registered (Phase 4+ image, Phase 5+ music/speech, Phase 3 safety), that are marked stub, or that the provider has deprecated. Each route carries an `available` boolean so callers can see what is missing, and deprecated routes carry a `deprecated` notice explaining what they now redirect to. Default false.

tools.name: build_ass_karaoke
tools.description: Build an ASS karaoke caption file from word-level timestamps. Pure transformer — accepts a `transcript_file` (e.g. `fal_transcribe` JSON output) OR an inline `words[]` array, plus optional style overrides. Each phrase gets one Dialogue event with per-word `\k<cs>` highlight timing summing to the event duration. Composes with `video_add_subtitles` for burn-in. See `ass_karaoke_prompt_guide` for color literal format and styling guidance.

transcript_file.description: Path or URI to a JSON transcript with word-level timing — `fal_transcribe` output works directly. Reads top-level `words[]` or nested `data.words[]`. Each word entry must have `text`, `start`, `end`. Scribe v2 `type: "spacing"` and `type: "audio_event"` entries are filtered out automatically. Mutually exclusive with `words`.

words.description: Inline word-level timestamps when the caller already has them in memory. Each word: `{text, start, end}` in seconds. Mutually exclusive with `transcript_file`. Caller is responsible for filtering non-spoken tokens.

output.description: Output URI for the ASS file (e.g., "./subs.ass", "gs://bucket/subs.ass"). The .ass extension is conventional but not enforced.

max_words_per_phrase.description: Maximum words shown on screen at once. Default 3 (reads cleanly on 9:16). 4–5 works on 16:9. Punctuation always forces a phrase break regardless.

font_name.description: Font family. Default "DM Sans". Must be installed on the rendering host (artificer / ffmpeg).

font_size.description: Font size in ASS units (relative to PlayResY). Default 96 (~9% of a 1080-wide phone frame).

unhighlighted_color.description: ASS color (`&HAABBGGRR`) for words not yet highlighted (`SecondaryColour`). Default "&H00FFFFFF" (opaque white). Alpha 00 = opaque, FF = transparent — note the inversion.

highlighted_color.description: ASS color for words once their karaoke time arrives (`PrimaryColour`). Default "&H005B44B0" (brand accent #b0445b).

outline_thickness.description: Outline thickness in pixels. Default 6 — heavy enough to stay legible on busy backgrounds.

margin_v.description: Vertical margin from frame bottom (Alignment=2). Default 240 — lifts captions out of TikTok's bottom-UI overlap zone.
